correctness.rationale: The exact binary block identity is proved by counting first-block, second-block and cross-block inversions; A and B are shown even, yielding the modulo-four congruence. Zolotarev and full Jacobi character orthogonality finish the exact evaluation. Independently recomputed direct inversion counts for all odd q from 3 through 139 (3994 units). The unrestricted conclusion is proved algebraically.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison with the originating paper separates its even-modulus parity theorem and odd-modulus root theorem from the present pointwise mod-four congruence and exact fourth-root spectrum. Targeted variant searches uncovered no covering theorem; the assessment has historical-priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not proven by negative indexing searches; an equivalent modular-inversion formula may appear in older permutation-statistics literature.
The original paper proposes the fourth-root zero case, so originality rests on a proof and the stronger exact distribution, not on identifying a novel conjectural zero.

value.rationale: The complete twice-odd modulus family, including all composite squares and nonsquares, is a motivated natural case of a published cyclotomic-factor conjecture. The stronger pointwise congruence yields an exact coefficient-class distribution and sharp zero criterion; it is not an arbitrary small numerical example.
